study type: Cross-sectional survey within a randomized trial
cohort: The study included 3604 women who answered an online Childbirth Experience Questionnaire four weeks after delivery, selected from 5810 women participating in the Labor Progression Study (LaPS-NCT02221427).
finding: Individual sociodemographic factors did not impact overall childbirth experience, but smoking was associated with a lower score on the professional support subscale, and delivery in week 37 was associated with a better overall childbirth experience.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery did not significantly influence the overall childbirth experience or its subscales.
gest_age: N/A (gestational age was an exposure, but no specific inclusion range was mentioned for the cohort)
